findings.title: No-drive model defaults are presented as best risk
findings.mechanism: The no-usable-drive service branch returns risk_score=0 and frequency/severity/loss-cost=1 with insufficient quality. The page forwards these finite defaults as valid model values, labels 0 best and applies positive tone; it does not condition model validity on drive_count/quality. Quality text below does not make these uncomputed readings measured zero.

steps: Trace the service branch with zero completed usable drives.
Its non-null response reaches the risk metric: displayed 0, best hint and positive tone, with baseline indices 1. No runtime render was executed.

findings.fix: Keep a real zero exposure/count separate from an uncomputed risk model. Preserve raw response but present model outputs as not computed with neutral tone and explicit insufficient-data reason.

findings.title: Peer/history percentile is not computed from a population
findings.mechanism: The service sets PeerPercentile to clamp(RiskScore,0,100), without a peer cohort, rank, history distribution or denominator. The page calls that value Peer percentile and Against your own history distribution.

steps: Read assignment PeerPercentile=clamp(RiskScore).
A synthetic risk score of 35 is labelled a history/peer percentile of 35 although no population comparison was performed.

findings.fix: Do not claim peer/history comparison. Mark percentile unavailable or label the returned score-derived proxy accurately until a real population contract exists.

findings.title: Confidence fraction is displayed as a percent without scaling
findings.mechanism: riskLevers emits confidence in [0.45,0.95]; formatPct appends % without multiplying. A confidence of 0.70 therefore reads 0.7%, not 70%. The page test uses an unrealistic confidence=70 fixture, so its declared table coverage does not exercise the production contract.

steps: Follow a source confidence fraction of 0.70 into formatPct.
The formatter emits the number 0.70 plus %, with precision preference controlling trailing digits.

findings.fix: Retain the raw fraction; scale only the displayed percentage by 100 and add fraction-shaped covering fixtures when tests are authorized.

findings.title: Risk-score point delta is rendered as percentage
findings.mechanism: The model computes projected_score_delta=(improvedDeviation-factor.Score)*weight*50, an additive delta on the 0-100 risk-score scale. The renderer adds % via formatSignedPct. Its -Math.abs also overwrites a future positive sign, although current production improvement deltas are non-positive; the latter is a candidate rather than evidence of a current sign reversal.

steps: A synthetic additive score delta of -4 is rendered as -4%.
That is four score points, not a relative percent change; exported raw delta remains -4.

findings.fix: Display localized signed score points and preserve the source sign. Do not change the raw export or confuse target_reduction_pct with score delta.

findings.title: Factor score uses unreachable overall-risk thresholds
findings.mechanism: Factor.Score is a signed bounded deviation in [-1,3], with positive meaning worse than baseline. Thresholds 35/60 copied from the overall 0-100 score are unreachable, so even maximum worsening deviation 3 is always green.

steps: Read factorDeviation clamp(-1,3).
For any valid positive factor score, both UI comparisons are false and green is selected.

findings.fix: Use the documented signed factor-deviation semantics for restrained neutral/worsening/improving presentation, not overall-risk thresholds; keep the numeric value and direction text.

findings.title: Evidence digest overclaims dataset/exposure coverage
findings.mechanism: The page claims a content hash over exposure, factors and window proving the same dataset. insuranceDigest hashes vehicle ID, window bounds, four rounded indices and factor code/rounded observed rate only. It omits exposure distance/duration, drive IDs/counts, factor samples, policy and model assumptions; it is not a complete evidence-packet or verified identity signature.

steps: Consider two synthetic profile structures with identical hashed fields but different exposure_distance_m or sample_count.
The digest serialization never reads those differing fields, so both digests are identical despite differing datasets. No digest function was executed.

findings.fix: Describe the existing digest as a limited risk-summary checksum, explicitly not verified identity or full dataset equality; any complete versioned digest needs separate domain ownership.

findings.title: Ownership dates bypass saved locale and timezone
findings.mechanism: The page trend/coverage, OwnershipBrief bounds/freshness and EvidencePanel observation dates call lib dateFormat without options. Those helpers default to browser locale/timezone, not saved preferences. Trend labels additionally memoize only data.trend, excluding a preference-bound formatter. Raw ISO timestamps remain intact, but interpreted labels can show a different day/zone and do not react correctly to preference changes.

steps: Choose synthetic ISO 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z with saved UTC/fr-FR and a browser in America/Los_Angeles/en-US.
Trace unconfigured lib calls: they use browser defaults rather than the saved settings. No settings were actually changed.

findings.fix: Use existing useDateFormat for page and shared ownership adapters; include its formatter in memo dependencies and make the applicable zone explicit without rewriting UTC source/form instants.

findings.title: Editor accepts maximum discounts the service rejects
findings.mechanism: The number input declares max=100 but UpsertInsurancePolicy rejects max_discount_pct>60. Native validity therefore accepts a 61-100 value that the server rejects; the failed draft is retained but advertised bounds are wrong.

steps: Inspect a synthetic max_discount_pct=75.
It lies within the JSX 0..100 constraint and outside the actual service 0..60 validation. No submission was executed.

findings.fix: Align form constraints/help to the supported 0..60 contract and provide localized validation. Preserve the existing rejection/draft lifecycle.

findings.title: Night distance is an undisclosed UTC trip-start proxy
findings.mechanism: observeRisk adds the entire drive distance when its StartedAt UTC hour is >=22 or <5. It does not measure distance actually driven at night or use local time. The page places it in Recorded driving exposure and labels it Night distance without disclosing that proxy.

steps: Reason about a synthetic 21:59Z departure spanning midnight: none of its distance is counted.
A 22:00Z departure contributes all distance even after daylight; local-zone night is not considered. No drive records were read or created.

findings.fix: Label the returned measure as distance of trips starting in the UTC overnight band, with proxy/bounds explanation; actual night-distance measurement requires separately owned model support.

findings.title: Dated insurance report cannot consume both workspace date bounds
findings.mechanism: The page owns a local 30/90/180/365 day selector. The hook key/URL contain vehicle_id and window_days only; the route is absent from RANGE_ENABLED_PATHS. Returned window.from/to are displayed but are not requested shared startInstant/endInstantExclusive bounds. This is a missing integration, not proof of two simultaneously visible pickers.

steps: Inspect /ownership/insurance-telematics against the exact range-enabled set and hook arguments.
A custom requested historical start/end range has no parameter path to this report; only a rolling day count is accepted. No URL navigation or request occurred.

findings.fix: Reuse inventory G152/P284 integration: establish typed server filtering for both bounds while preserving rolling windows, then integrate the existing workspace owner. Do not filter loaded rows or simply register a non-consuming route.

findings.title: Policy writes omit the existing live-mode guard
findings.mechanism: PUT/DELETE insurance policy request options omit requiresLiveMode. request defaults it to false and assertOperationalWriteAllowed returns immediately when false. Page actions check selected vehicle/pending/editor state, not operational read-only mode; offlineUnsafePatterns do not include insurance-telematics. QueryClient mutation defaults do prevent queued replay, so this is guard omission, not a proven offline queue/replay bug or backend authorization bypass.

steps: Trace PUT/DELETE options with a hypothetical historical/offline operational snapshot.
requiresLiveMode is false, so the client live-mode check is bypassed. No mutation, network request or backend authorization check was executed.

findings.fix: Opt both policy mutations into the existing requiresLiveMode protection and make disabled/recovery reasons truthful through the existing operational-mode owner; preserve confirmation, no-replay defaults and context pinning.

findings.mechanism: The page has 951 lines with multiple sections, form handlers and both table column definitions; applicable frontend instructions prohibit page files over 300 lines. It was already 845 lines before Phase5; this is inherited architectural debt, not evidence of deleted functionality.

steps: Compare the actual 951-line source with the documented 300-line page limit.

findings.fix: Parent may authorize a separate exclusive decomposition claim, preserving all sections/actions/15 raw metrics/tests. This read-only audit authorizes no extraction or helper creation.
